hook: Content note: the page opens with an adult content warning covering sexual assault, child abuse, gore, self-harm, suicide and torture, and the file earns every item on that list. It concerns a captive girl held by the Foundation, and much of its weight comes from what is withheld through redactions and implication. If that is not something you want to sit with, skipping it is entirely reasonable.
whyItMatters: It is the starkest version of the Foundation's necessary-evil theme: the containment procedure itself is the atrocity, and the file never lets the reader off the hook about who carries it out. It also brings in the Scarlet King and the cult that worships him, a name the poems in the margins keep returning to.
thingsToNotice:
The seven subjects were rescued from a cult's warehouse, all pregnant with the King's offspring, and each of the first six died in a way that let a catastrophic event loose: childbirth, a forced removal of the fetus, suicide with a surgeon's knife, a failed cure, a botched procedure that levelled a site, and a stray bullet during a rescue attempt. Procedure 110-Montauk is never spelled out, but the clues are deliberate: six Class-D personnel assigned to it every month, a ban on violent criminals because they might kill her, a girl strapped to a bed and denied painkillers, a memo admitting it involves brutal acts, and a verse calling her defiled all point to repeated sexual violence used to keep the birth from happening.

The O5 memo insists she is not being abandoned, and an unsigned line right after it says the Foundation has exactly what it wants. When her distress starts fading, the solution is to wipe her memory mid-procedure so the terror stays fresh; the doctor who proposed it shoots himself, and his successor calmly tunes the amnestic schedule to once a week for peak dread. The lowercase nursery-rhyme verses woven through the record tell the same events from the cult's side and predict that the seventh bride will birth the end of time.
